scenes.narration: Your app emails a sign-in code. Your test reads it, with no mailbox. By the end, a test signs in on Android and iOS by itself.
Tests cannot open your inbox. So teams share a test account and wait. In Shipvo, every session has its own private inbox, with its own address.
Step one. Ask for the address. The tool is inbox read. Type that address into the app's email field.
scenes.caption: Step one. Ask for the address. The tool is inbox_read. Type that address into the app's email field.

scenes.narration: Step two. Tap send code. The app sends its mail to the session inbox. A mock network rule can send it too.
Step three. Wait for the mail. Inbox wait returns the sender, the subject, and the code. Four eight two nine one three.
scenes.caption: Step three. Wait for the mail. inbox_wait returns the sender, the subject, and the code: 482913.

scenes.narration: Step four. Type the code and tap verify. The app says welcome back. You are signed in.
It works the same on Android and iOS. Open the session with platform android, or platform iOS.
What if no mail comes? You do not hang. You get a typed error, inbox timeout, and you can read what did arrive.
scenes.caption: What if no mail comes? You do not hang. You get a typed error, inbox_timeout, and you can read what did arrive.

scenes.narration: In a typed test, it is three lines. Address, send, code. For a magic link, open the first link in the mail.
Test the sign-in, and skip the mailbox. Read the guide at shipvo dot dev, slash docs, slash email dash sign dash in.
scenes.caption: Test the sign-in, and skip the mailbox. Read the guide at shipvo.dev/docs/email-sign-in.
